glossary.definition: An LLM key that reaches Bedrock under an assumed IAM role and stores no provider credential. Metering, AI Guard and audit stay intact on the call, and the same route also works as a fallback target. These are the claims taken from the 2026-11-21 release notes; everything about how the lab shows them is its own model.

The policy on the role that says who may assume it. In the lab an Allow must name the principal the gateway presents, a Deny wins, and an optional external-ID condition is compared exactly. The lab reads a small subset of IAM as data and never evaluates policy text as code.

The policy on the role that says what it may do once assumed. The lab checks one action, bedrock:InvokeModel, on the model's ARN. Identity-side permissions, service control policies and permission boundaries are not modelled.

A value the trust policy can require and the key must carry. The lab compares it exactly and case-sensitively; an empty one counts as none. Missing and mismatched are two different named results with different fixes.

Every way the role assumption or the invoke can fail has its own code, title and fix: wrong trust principal, external ID missing or mismatched, missing invoke permission, model not enabled in the region, expired session. The wording is the lab's own and UNVERIFIED.

On Vertex AI the gateway uses its own service account: no role is assumed, there is no external ID and no session. The lab needs a binding to a role that grants aiplatform.endpoints.predict (roles/aiplatform.user or roles/aiplatform.admin). The role model is the lab's own and UNVERIFIED.

Anything the release notes do not say is the lab's own model and is labelled UNVERIFIED: the console setup fields, the session length, every error text, the order of the checks, the principal the gateway presents, and whether an expired session refreshes by itself.

cards.label: S01: The role is assumed and the call is served
cards.description: The key names a role. The gateway assumes it, the call is served, and the trace still shows the guard, metering and audit hops, all done.

cards.label: S02: The trust policy names someone else
cards.description: The result is named: Wrong trust principal, with its fix. Nothing is invoked or metered and the refusal is audited.

cards.label: S03: The external ID does not match
cards.description: The result is External ID mismatch, with the fix: make the key's external ID equal the trust policy's value.

cards.label: S04: The external ID was never set
cards.description: The result is External ID missing, and it is a different result from a mismatch, so the fix is different too.

cards.label: S05: The role cannot invoke the model
cards.description: The trace shows the assume succeeded and the invoke failed. The fix is to allow the invoke on the model for the guest services platform team's role.

cards.label: S06: The model is not enabled in that region
cards.description: The result names the region problem and its fix: enable the model there, or point the key at a region where it is enabled.

cards.label: S07: The session expires and is refreshed
cards.description: The clock reaches the expiry exactly; the next call assumes the role again and is served as session_refreshed on a new session.

cards.label: S08: AI Guard still applies to this key
cards.description: A prompt carrying the stub guard's marker is blocked before any role is assumed. No session, no invoke, no metering, and the block is audited.

cards.label: S09: The key with no credential, next to the key with one
cards.description: The stored key shows a mask; the assumed-role key has no credential field at all, at any depth. Both are metered, guarded and audited the same way.

cards.label: S10: The assumed-role key serves as a fallback
cards.description: The assumed-role key is the second target and serves, still metered, guarded and audited. The chain logic belongs to the fallback lab.

cards.label: S11: Vertex AI: the service account has the role
cards.description: A binding to a role that grants the predict permission lets the call through.

cards.label: S12: Vertex AI: the service account has no role
cards.description: The result is Service account has no role, with the fix: bind a role that grants the permission.

cards.label: S13: Vertex AI: a role that does not grant the call
cards.description: The result is Role does not grant the call, a different result from having no role at all.

cards.label: What is sourced and what is the lab's model
cards.description: The release-notes claims, the lab's own model and the list of what is UNVERIFIED.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
